source_text: Ταύτας τὰς κατηριθμημένας τοῦ πνεύματος δυνάμεις οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεοῦς αὐτοῦ τούτων ὄντος φησὶν ὁ λόγος ἐπεληλυθέναι ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, ἀλλ᾿ ὡς ἐπ᾿ ἐκεῖνον ἀνάπαυσιν μελλουσῶν ποιεῖσθαι, τουτέστιν ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πέρας ποιεῖσθαι, τοῦ μηκέτι ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν κατὰ τὸ παλαιὸν ἔθος προφήτας γενήσεσθαι, ὅπερ καὶ ὄψει ὑμῖν ἰδεῖν ἔστι· μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον γὰρ οὐδεὶς ὅλως προφήτης παρ᾿ ὑμῖν γεγένηται.
pass_a_gloss: The Word says these enumerated powers of the Spirit came upon Him not as if He was in need of them, but as to bring rest to the things that were to be done upon Him, that is to bring an end to Him, so that there would no longer be prophets among your race according to the old custom, which you will also see for yourselves; for after Him, no prophet has arisen among you

choices.english: that is, to bring an end to the old custom
rejected: to bring an end to Him

choices.term: μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον γὰρ οὐδεὶς ὅλως προφήτης παρ᾿ ὑμῖν γεγένηται
choices.english: for after Him, no prophet has arisen among you
rejected: for after Him, not a single prophet has arisen among you

pass_b_english: The Word tells us that the Spirit's powers, which are listed here, came upon Him, but not because He needed them. Instead, they came to bring a sense of completion to the work that was being done through Him. In other words, with His arrival, a new era began, one in which prophets would no longer arise among your people, as had been the custom in the past. You can see this for yourselves: after Him, there hasn't been a single prophet to emerge from among you.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: Pass A contains a significant mistranslation of the Greek clause 'τουτέστιν ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πέρας ποιεῖσθαι'. Pass A translates this as 'that is to bring an end to Him', whereas the Greek 'ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πέρας ποιεῖσθαι' in this context refers to bringing an end to the era/process of prophecy (as correctly noted in the 'choices' lemma section: 'to bring an end to the old custom'). Pass A's rendering 'bring an end to Him' changes the theological meaning from the cessation of a function to the termination of the person. Pass B is a paraphrase rather than a translation, but Pass A's error is a direct fidelity failure.
reasons: Pass A mistranslates 'τουτέστιν ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πέρας ποιεῖσθαι' as 'that is to bring an end to Him', which contradicts the Greek sense of bringing an end to the prophetic era/custom (πέρας ποιεῖσθαι... τοῦ μηκέτι... προφήτας γενήσεσθαι).
